This section examines Chapter 6 — XOR
walkthrough (5–6 minutes)

from first principles. Keep two questions
separate: does changing the

order change the measured outcome, and
does the proposed search

method beat a matched alternative at the
same distinct-evaluation budget?

Reconstruct one search story from
initialization to breakthrough: generate

20 random orderings; evaluate each
candidate network; show a tournament

of three; preserve the elite; perform a
swap; track diversity

falling over generations; show an extended
accuracy plateau; animate a

critical mutation producing a perfect XOR
ordering near the reported

100–150-generation range. Explicitly
explain that the plotted trajectory is

an explanatory example of the mechanism
and must not be

used to erase the reproduction correction
that noisy historical best-ever

fitness could be inflated. The distinction
is part of the

result. A large ordering effect does not
automatically imply an

evolutionary-search advantage, and
almost-sure convergence does not promise
